stories.title: Burnham's Approval Rating Drops by Six Points
stories.summary: More in Common's tracker shows PM Andy Burnham's net approval has fallen from +20 to +14 points — still above all other party leaders. Kemi Badenoch is now at +1, while Reform's Farage-ally Polanski sits at a joint-low of -29.

stories.title: UK Economy Grew by Only 0.4% in Q2 — Burnham Warned of Risks
stories.summary: GDP grew 0.4% between April and June, but PM Burnham has been warned growth could stall next year if Strait of Hormuz disruption continues. The figures add pressure on the new government's economic credibility.

stories.title: "Angry" Burnham Attacks Water Companies Over Bill Increases
stories.summary: PM Burnham publicly expressed anger at water companies following reports of large bill increases for consumers, signalling the government may take a harder line with the water sector.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🤖 Unemployed Young People to Join AI Boot Camps to Get Job-Ready
stories.summary: The Burnham government is launching AI boot camps for unemployed young people, aiming to equip them with skills for AI-driven job markets. This signals a major digital skills investment push as part of the government's growth agenda.

stories.title: 🤖 Stephanie Peacock Confirmed as Digital Government Minister
stories.summary: Barnsley South MP Stephanie Peacock has been confirmed as the new Minister for Digital Government within the expanded DCMS, replacing Ian Murray following Andy Burnham's machinery of government changes. Her first public-facing role covers GOV.UK App promotion for A-level results day.

stories.title: 🤖 HMRC Offers £100k for Senior Manager to Oversee AI Deployment
stories.summary: HMRC is advertising a senior manager role at £100k to lead the 'safe and effective deployment of AI' across the department, reflecting the government's push to embed AI in core tax and revenue functions.

topics.description: House of Commons, House of Lords, PMQs, debates, legislation

stories.title: Education Secretary Makes Grammatical Mistakes in A-Level Results Statement
stories.summary: The Education Secretary drew ridicule after making grammatical errors in an official statement about A-Level results day, creating an embarrassing moment for the new Burnham government.

stories.title: Burnham Moves 40 Illegal Migrants Into Councils That Had None
stories.summary: Controversy is growing after reports that 40 local authorities which previously had no illegal migrants have been assigned allocations under the Burnham government's migration dispersal policy.

stories.title: Kemi Badenoch's Approval Rating Rises to +1
stories.summary: Kemi Badenoch's net approval rating as Conservative leader has improved significantly over the past 12 months, reaching +1 according to More in Common tracking — though this has not translated to improved overall party ratings.

stories.title: Questions Over Badenoch Giving Former Neo-Nazi an Advisory Role
stories.summary: Kemi Badenoch is facing scrutiny after The Guardian raised questions about why she appointed a person with a former neo-Nazi background to an advisory role in the Conservative Party.

stories.title: Ed Davey Urges All Parties to Deny Farage Oxygen in Clacton
stories.summary: Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey called for all parties to 'stand aside and refuse to give oxygen to Farage's vanity project' ahead of the Clacton by-election — which Farage had himself triggered by resigning his seat.

topics.description: Nigel Farage, party news and announcements

stories.title: Farage Wins Clacton By-Election With 22,239 Votes — But Doesn't Attend Count
stories.summary: Nigel Farage won the Clacton by-election with 22,239 votes (turnout 44.37%), with Count Binface second on 9,455. Farage controversially refused to attend the result declaration, citing security concerns — but Essex Police denied advising him to stay away.

stories.title: Farage Under Investigation Over £5m Undeclared Gift as He Returns to Commons
stories.summary: Despite his by-election victory, Farage continues to face a parliamentary investigation into a £5 million gift he received but did not declare. He responded to questions about this by saying 'the voters of Clacton don't care'.

stories.title: Reform Cancels Farage's Post-Victory 'Major Speech' in Clacton
stories.summary: Reform UK cancelled a planned 'major speech' by Farage in Clacton on the morning after the by-election, giving no reason. The move came amid chaotic scenes over his decision to skip the count declaration.

stories.title: Swinney Challenges Burnham on Vetoed Chinese Wind Turbine Factory Plan
stories.summary: Scottish First Minister John Swinney was praised for being 'absolutely right' to challenge Andy Burnham over the UK Government's block on a Chinese firm's plans to build a wind turbine factory in Scotland, raising tensions over devolved economic decisions.

stories.title: Ex-SpAd Tells Sturgeon and Joanna Cherry to End 'Tedious' Feud
stories.summary: Kate Higgins, who advised three Scottish First Ministers, publicly rebuked Nicola Sturgeon, Joanna Cherry, and JK Rowling over their ongoing Fringe-fuelled feud, calling on them to move on for the good of Scottish politics.

stories.title: Stephanie Peacock Takes on Digital Government Brief in Ministerial Reshuffle
stories.summary: Following Andy Burnham's machinery of government changes that expanded DCMS, Stephanie Peacock (MP for Barnsley South) has been formally confirmed as Minister for Digital Government, taking over from Ian Murray whose full portfolio is yet to be confirmed.

stories.title: Clacton By-Election Result: Farage 22,239 — Count Binface 9,455
stories.summary: Nigel Farage won the Clacton by-election he triggered by resigning his seat, with 22,239 votes to Count Binface's 9,455. All major parties stood aside, making it a protest vote arena. The result confirms Farage will return to the Commons.

stories.title: A String of Dramatic By-Elections Since 2024: The Full Context
stories.summary: The Clacton result is the latest in a run of high-profile by-elections since 2024: Reform won Runcorn & Helsby; Greens won Gorton & Denton; the SNP held Arbroath; Conservatives took Aberdeen South; and Burnham won Makerfield to become PM.
